facts.fact: The delegated civil-registry officer of Ratoma commune says his office goes on registering births in the digital civil-registration system, which runs from a data centre held elsewhere (formerly at the Maison centrale), while printing is stopped for want of secure paper (reported 2 September 2026).
facts.system: actes de naissance numériques (digital civil registration)

facts.fact: The Ratoma officer says the secure paper serves to issue digital birth certificates 'in all the communes of Guinea' and the report says several communes share the stockout; no count of communes working in the system is given (2 September 2026).
facts.system: actes de naissance numériques (digital civil registration)

facts.fact: The relocation of the data centre from the Maison centrale disrupted the digital civil-registration system used by commune offices, with engineers reinstalling it at a new site and service expected back within the week, on top of a stockout of secure paper lasting about two weeks (reported 2 September 2026).
facts.system: actes de naissance numériques (digital civil registration)

systems.system: Digital civil registration (actes de naissance numériques)
systems.owner: a contracted company supplies the secure paper and runs the data centre; not named
systems.tiers: commune civil-registry offices; Ratoma named, 'all the communes of Guinea' in the officer's words

systems.system: Data centre of the digital civil-registration system
systems.tiers: moved from the Maison centrale to new premises, September 2026

note: The connection is read from the office working in a system hosted elsewhere; the document does not say how the commune office is connected or who pays for it.
